hypotheses.justification: The statement does not use this instance. `translationAlgEquivOf` (line 7496, section UnconditionalAut, whose variables are only `{W} (hΔ) {a b} (hA)`) does not take it. `addXFun` (a private def in the velu_map_equation file, line 6588, with variables only `{F} [Field F] (W) (a b)`), `negY` and `polyToFunctionField` do not take it either. It is an argument only because it is instance-implicit and `F` is an argument. In the proof, the only lemma that needs it is `addXFun_ne_algebraMap hΔ hA` (line 5379, section NonDegeneracy with `[DecidableEq F]`). That lemma's conclusion `W.addXFun a b ≠ ι a` does not depend on the instance, so a proof starting with `classical` can supply it, which is how that lemma's own proof begins. The other lemmas used (`addFun_neg_cancel_X`, `translationAlgEquivOf_polyToFunctionField_X`, `translationAlgEquivOf_yGen`, `polyToFunctionField_X_ne_algebraMap`) come from sections without `DecidableEq F`. So the theorem stays true and provable with `omit [DecidableEq F] in` and `classical` added at the start of the proof.
